messages.author: Kankana Bhattacharjee
messages.body:
Dear AMBER users,
I am trying to run QMMM calculation using sander.quick.cuda utility. I have
used this command lin:
sander.quick.cuda -O -i qmmm.in -o qmmm.out -p lig-solv-qmmm.prmtop -c
equil.rst -r qmmm.rst -x qmmm.mdcrd
But, getting this error: cudaGetDeviceCount gpu_init failed!: CUDA driver
version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version in
/apps/scratch/compile/amber22-gpu-quick/amber22_src/AmberTools/src/quick/src/cuda/
gpu.cu at line 80
It seems the current installed cuda version is incompatible with the cuda
which is required for sander.quick.cuda. Kindly suggest how can I fix this
?
I am sharing my job script which is using for running
the sander.quick.cuda.
Kindly help.
Thanks & Regards
Kankana Bhattacharjee

messages.author: Timothy Giese
messages.body:
"It seems the current installed cuda version is incompatible with the cuda
which is required for sander.quick.cuda. Kindly suggest how can I fix this?"
This cannot be fixed by adjusting your amber input files. As you appear to understand, you will need to install a more recent cuda version. You will need to contact your local computer administrator to install it for you, or you could try to install and configure it yourself. Here is a link to nvidia's website with instructions on how to install cuda. The nvidia website also contains a forum where you can ask for additional help on how to install cuda.
https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-installation-guide-linux/

messages.author: Goetz, Andreas
messages.body:
As Tim pointed out this error is not related to QUICK or Amber.
The CUDA driver installed on the computer you are trying to run the simulations is too old for the CUDA version that you used to compile Amber. You have to upgrade the CUDA driver or use an older CUDA development toolkit for compilation and runtime.
All the best,
Andy
